newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil's Heidrun oilfield pumping at 220,000 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Statoil's Heidrun oilfield pumping at 220,000 bpd.

text.p: Oil output at the Heidrun oilfield in the Norwegian Sea was back to just over 220,000 barrels per day (bpd) following an 11-day maintenance shutdown, operator Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap ASA (Statoil) said on Monday.
"On Sunday Heidrun produced nearly 35,000 cubic metres (220,150 barrels)," Statoil spokesman Odd Jan Lange said.
Heidrun was shut for turnaround on September 2 and restarted oil production on Friday.
In August the field produced an average 232,440 bpd. Output has exceeded 250,000 bpd but Statoil reduced pumping due to problems at water injector wells.
"We're about to finish cleaning up the water injector wells. The work should be completed in the next few days and then, hopefully, we will be back to 250,000 bpd," Lange said.
